title: Steamed Manila Clams with Udon
chef: Larry Tse, The House, San Francisco
ingredients: 1 tablespoon instant hon dashi (soup stock) granules
1 leek, white part only, coarsely chopped
2 cups firmly packed katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes)
2 (3 1/2-ounce) packages enoki mushrooms, roots trimmed and separated into small bunches
1 bunch fresh chives, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 sheets toasted nori, cut into 1-by-1/4-inch strips
method: Heat the 2 1/2 quarts water to just short of boiling, then take it off the heat.
Wipe the kombu lightly with a cloth and add it to the hot water with the dashi granules and soy sauce; leave 30 minutes.
Put the pan back over medium-high heat, add the leek and bring to a boil, then simmer gently on low for 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the bonito flakes and let them steep 15 minutes. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean pan and salt to taste if needed.
Boil the 4 cups water in a wide pan, add the clams, cover and steam about 3 minutes, shaking now and then, until they open.
Lift out the clams, throwing away any that stay shut, and discard the cooking liquid. Pick the meat from the shells.
Boil the udon as the packet directs and drain.
Bring the broth back to a boil, take it off the heat and add the clam meat and enoki.
Share the noodles among bowls, ladle the broth, clams and mushrooms over, top with chives and nori strips and serve right away.

title: Grilled Snapper with Root Vegetable Salad
chef: Lachlan M. Patterson, Frasca Food and Wine, Boulder
ingredients: Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
1 head flowering kale or small bunch regular kale
method: Heat a grill for direct cooking over medium heat.
Rub the snapper all over with 1/4 cup of the oil and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Peel the turnips, celery root, beets and parsnips. Slice each paper-thin on a mandoline, then cut into very fine julienne (or shred on a box grater or in a processor).
Trim the radicchio and kale and shred the leaves very finely.
Combine all the vegetables with the shallots and chives, dress with the remaining 1/2 cup oil and 3/4 cup of the lemon juice, season and toss.
Oil the grill rack and cook the fish about 3 minutes per side, turning once, until marked and just opaque in the middle.
Plate the fish on warm plates, drizzle with the rest of the lemon juice and serve with the salad.

title: Filet Bean and Scallop Salad
chef: Anne S. Quatrano, Bacchanalia, Atlanta
ingredients: 1 pound Nickel filet beans or other small, slender green beans, stem ends trimmed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 sea scallops (about 1 pound total weight), preferably diver
method: Blanch the beans in boiling salted water about 30 seconds until tender-crisp, chill in ice water, drain well and set aside.
For the dressing, mix the vinegar and shallots, add the honey, then whisk in the hazelnut oil and 1 tablespoon grape seed oil in a thin stream. Season.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan over low heat 3 to 4 minutes, shaking, until golden. Cool and chop roughly.
Heat the remaining tablespoon of grape seed oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Dry and season the scallops, then sear about 2 minutes per side, turning once, until just translucent in the centre.
Set 2 scallops on each warm plate. Toss the beans with the dressing and scatter them over the scallops.
Finish with the hazelnuts and chervil and serve immediately.

title: Mushroom Salad with Warm Goat Cheese Toasts
chef: Loretta Keller, COCO500 and the Moss Room, San Francisco
ingredients: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 pound fresh goat cheese, at room temperature
method: Slice the mushrooms thinly and fold them gently with the crème fraîche, lemon juice, zest and a pinch of salt and pepper.
String the celery with a peeler, slice it thinly across and mix it into the mushrooms.
Toast the bread, brush one side with the oil and rub that side with the cut garlic.
Spread a quarter of the goat cheese on each toast.
Quickly toss the herbs, arugula and mâche with the oil and lemon juice, then season.
Divide the mushroom salad among 4 plates, top with the herb salad and set a warm cheese toast alongside. Serve at once.

title: Grilled Branzino with Heirloom-Tomato Panzanella
chef: Ethan Stowell, Union / Tavolàta / How to Cook a Wolf, Seattle
ingredients: 3 (1-pound) whole branzino, filleted with skin intact (see note)
Extra virgin olive oil for brushing
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 pound day-old ciabatta or other crusty coarse country bread, cut into 1-inch cubes (about 3 cups)
2 large heirloom or other good-quality tomatoes (about 1/2 pound each), cut into 1-inch cubes
1/2 cup peeled, seeded, and diced cucumber
10 fresh basil leaves, torn into small pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat a grill for direct cooking over medium heat. Brush the 6 fillets with oil on both sides and season.
For the panzanella, mix the bread, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, oil, vinegar and basil, season, and let sit 5 to 10 minutes so the bread soaks up the dressing.
Oil the grill rack and cook the fillets skin side down 3 to 4 minutes until the skin crisps.
Flip carefully and grill another 2 to 3 minutes, just until opaque in the centre.
Spoon the panzanella onto 6 plates, lay the fish on top and pour over any dressing left in the bowl. Serve straight away.
If branzino is unavailable, six 4-ounce halibut fillets can be used instead; check fillets for pin bones.

title: Vegetable Pot-au-Feu with Toasted Spice Broth
chef: Floyd Cardoz, Tabla, New York
ingredients: 18 small shallots or pearl onions, unpeeled
1 head garlic, separated into cloves, unpeeled
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes (about 3 cups)
1-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced across the grain
1 cup diced, peeled butternut squash (1/2-inch dice)
1/2 cup pink lentils, picked over, rinsed, soaked in cold water to cover for 30 minutes, and drained
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Wrap the shallots and garlic in a foil parcel with 1 tablespoon oil, salt and pepper.
Toss the turnips and carrots with the other 2 tablespoons oil and seasoning on a small rimmed tray. Roast tray and parcel about 25 minutes until tender; peel the cooled shallots and garlic.
Boil the potatoes in lightly salted water about 20 minutes until tender, drain, cool a little and quarter.
For the broth, dry-roast the crushed garlic and ginger in a heavy 4-quart pan over medium heat about 10 minutes until lightly coloured.
Add the squash, lentils and stock and simmer about 40 minutes until both are soft.
Toast the spice-mix spices in a small dry pan over low heat 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant and coloured; cool and grind finely.
Stir the ground spices into the broth and simmer 10 minutes. Cool slightly, pulse in batches to an oatmeal texture, push through a coarse sieve and salt to taste.
Heat the tablespoon of oil in a small pan until smoking, add the mustard seeds and cook about 30 seconds until they pop; tip into the broth.
Bring the broth to a simmer over medium-high heat with all the roasted vegetables, potatoes and edamame until heated through.
Stir in the lime juice and cilantro and serve in a warm bowl with steamed rice.

title: Veal Chops with Aligot
chef: Philippe Jeanty, Bistro Jeanty, Yountville
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 cup grated Cantal or tomme cheese
1/4 cup Marsanne or other dry white wine
method: Coat the chops in 1/2 cup of the oil in a glass dish, press a sage sprig, thyme sprig and garlic clove onto each, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Scrape off and discard the herbs and garlic and season the chops.
Heat the remaining 1/4 cup oil in a large ovenproof nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the chops and butter and brown about 3 minutes per side.
Move the skillet to the oven for about 10 minutes for medium, then rest the chops under loose foil for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the smooth mashed potatoes in a heavy pan over medium-low heat and stir in the cheese until melted and fondue-like, about 5 minutes (10 to 15 if the potatoes started cold).
Add the wine and garlic and keep stirring a few minutes more until the potatoes turn stretchy.
Spoon the aligot onto 4 warm plates, set a chop on each and serve. Pork chops of the same thickness can replace the veal.

title: Almond Cake with a Warm Red Berry–Vanilla Compote
chef: Emily Luchetti, Farallon and Waterbar, San Francisco
ingredients: 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
5 ounces almond paste, at room temperature
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
1 pint strawberries, hulled and quartered if small or cut into eighths if large
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 9-inch round pan and line the base with parchment.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together.
With a mixer on medium, beat the butter and almond paste about 1 minute until smooth, then beat in the sugar 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the eggs one by one, beating after each, then the vanilla. On low speed mix in the dry ingredients.
Spread in the pan and bake about 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool fully in the pan, then loosen, turn out, peel off the paper and set right side up.
For the compote, put the citrus juices, 1 tablespoon sugar, salt and scraped vanilla seeds in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute.
Melt in the butter (about 30 seconds), then add the berries and warm gently about 1 minute; don't let them collapse. Add sugar if needed.
Serve wedges of cake with a spoonful of the warm berries.

title: Hawaiian Burger with Pineapple–Macadamia Nut Relish
chef: Hubert Keller, Fleur de Lys and Burger Bar, San Francisco / Las Vegas
ingredients: 2 tablespoons fresh or canned finely diced water chestnuts
2 tablespoons coarsely chopped toasted macadamia nuts
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken thighs or ground dark-meat chicken
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, plus leaves for garnish
1 tablespoon finely grated, peeled fresh ginger
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Toasted unsweetened flaked coconut for garnish (optional)
method: Gently combine the relish ingredients, season, cover and chill.
If using thighs, cube them and pulse in a processor (or chop by hand) until coarsely ground.
Mix the chicken with the coconut milk, chopped cilantro, ginger, garlic and lime juice, season, cover and chill 30 minutes.
Heat a grill for direct cooking over medium heat. Form 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick and brush with the oil.
Grill on an oiled rack 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, toasting the buns cut side down for the last 1 to 2 minutes.
Build each burger on the bun base with lettuce, tomato and the patty, then top with relish, cilantro leaves and toasted coconut. Close and serve.

title: Ras el Hanout Crab Salad with Onion Rings
chef: Vikram Vij, Vij's, Vancouver
ingredients: 1 1/2 teaspoons ground ras el hanout (see note)
1 pound crabmeat, picked over for shell fragments and cartilage
1/4 cup loosely packed chopped fresh cilantro
1 teaspoon finely minced jalapeño chile, without seeds
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 small yellow onions, sliced 1/4 inch thick
method: Soften the shallots in the oil over low heat about 3 minutes, add the ras el hanout and cook 2 minutes more; let cool.
Fold the crab gently with the shallot mixture, coconut cream, lemon juice, cilantro and jalapeño, and season. Make no more than an hour ahead and keep chilled.
Separate the onion slices into rings. Beat the eggs in one bowl and put the flour in another.
Heat 1 inch of oil in a pan to 350°F.
Dip rings in egg, then flour, and fry in batches about 3 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain on paper towels and salt.
Spoon a small mound of crab onto serving spoons, top each with an onion ring and serve on a tray.

title: Lobster Cioppino
chef: Richard Vellante, Legal Sea Foods, Boston
ingredients: 1 cup diced canned tomatoes with juice
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup chopped roasted red bell pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 cup Roussanne or other dry white wine
2 tablespoons fresh basil leaves, torn into pieces
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Sweat the celery, carrot and onion in the oil over low heat about 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, clam broth and stock, simmer 5 minutes, season, add the bay leaf and thyme and simmer 5 minutes more. Remove the bay leaf; you need about 3 cups. It keeps 3 days chilled.
Purée the roasted pepper, garlic, parsley, lemon juice and paprika, blend in the mayonnaise, season and chill as the rouille.
Heat the oil in a soup pot over medium heat and cook the clams 2 minutes. Add the mussels and wine, cover and cook 3 to 5 minutes until the shells open.
Lift out the shellfish (discard unopened ones) and keep warm. Boil the wine uncovered about 3 minutes to reduce by half.
Add the 3 cups broth, bring to a simmer, add the lobsters, cover and cook 8 to 10 minutes until they start to redden.
Add the scallops and shrimp and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until just cooked. Stir in the basil and season.
Halve the lobsters lengthwise. Ring each warm soup plate with clams and mussels, add broth, scallops and shrimp, and set a lobster half in the middle.
Serve with bread, passing the rouille at the table.

title: Sherry-Roasted Figs with Crispy Streusel and Crème Fraîche
chef: Kate Zuckerman (Chanterelle, New York)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons firmly packed light brown sugar
4 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/4-inch cubes
2 orange peel strips, each about 3 inches long
method: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a rimmed tray with foil or parchment.
Fork together both sugars, the flour and salt, then cut in the cold butter with two knives until pea-sized or finer. Spread on the tray to dry.
Stem and halve the figs and set them cut side up in one layer in a snug nonreactive dish.
Dissolve 1/3 cup sugar in the sherry and pour into the dish with the orange peel.
Roast 10 minutes, baste, sprinkle with 1 tablespoon sugar; roast 10 minutes, baste and sprinkle with the last tablespoon; roast 10 minutes more until very soft but intact.
Discard the peel and leave the figs in their syrup (they keep a day in the fridge).
Lower the oven to 350°F. Bake the streusel 15 minutes, break up clumps, bake 10 to 15 minutes until lightly browned, break up again and bake 5 minutes. Cool completely.
Reheat the figs at 350°F about 10 minutes.
Serve 4 fig halves per plate with a tablespoon of syrup, a spoonful of crème fraîche and a generous scattering of streusel.

title: Peruvian Seafood Chowder
chef: Michelle Bernstein, Michy's and Sra. Martinez, Miami
ingredients: 2 pounds extra-large shrimp in the shell (about 24)
1/4 cup finely chopped red bell pepper
1/4 teaspoon minced habanero or Scotch Bonnet chile
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup finely diced, peeled sweet potato
1/4 cup finely diced tomato with juice
1/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh cilantro leaves and stems
4 large eggs, at room temperature, lightly beaten
method: Peel and devein the shrimp, keeping the shells; refrigerate the shrimp.
For the stock, fry the shells in the oil over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes until deep red, add the water, wine, bay and peppercorns, boil, then simmer gently about 20 minutes.
Strain, pressing the shells; top up with water to make 4 cups.
Cook the onion, bell pepper, fennel, garlic and chile in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat about 4 minutes, without browning.
Add the wine and reduce by half, about 3 minutes, scraping the pan. Add the stock and reduce by about half, 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir in the evaporated milk and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until thickened; season and keep warm.
Sear the seasoned shrimp in 3 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat about 2 minutes until pink and firm; set aside.
Add the last tablespoon of oil to the pan and cook the corn and sweet potato 2 minutes. Add the broth, scrape the pan and bring to a simmer.
Return the shrimp with the tomato and cilantro, season and heat through.
Off the heat, pour in the beaten eggs slowly while stirring so they set into ribbons, about 1 minute. Serve in warm bowls.

title: Louisiana Popcorn Rice and Wild Rice Pilaf with Crabmeat, Almonds, and Lemon
chef: Susan Spicer, Bayona, New Orleans
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons unsalted butter or olive oil
2 celery stalks with leaves, stalks finely diced and leaves chopped
Grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
1 pound jumbo lump blue crabmeat or Dungeness crabmeat, picked over for shells and cartilage
1/2 cup Trebbiano or other light-bodied white wine
2 1/2 cups chicken stock, vegetable stock, or water
1 bunch green onions, including tender green tops, thinly sliced
method: Rinse the wild rice well, add to the 3 cups boiling water with a little salt, cover and simmer over medium heat 25 to 40 minutes until split and tender but chewy. Drain and keep warm.
Halfway through, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion, diced celery, lemon zest and bay leaf 3 to 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the pecan rice (or basmati) to coat, then fold in half the crab and add the wine, stock, half the lemon juice and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low about 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Mix in the wild rice, season and remove the bay leaf.
Warm the rest of the crab gently in the remaining tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat; season with salt and the last of the lemon juice.
Plate the pilaf, top with the warm crab and scatter with celery leaves, almonds and green onions.

title: White Bean and Salt Cod Stew with Guindilla Peppers
chef: Gerald Hirigoyen, Piperade and Bocadillos, San Francisco
ingredients: 2 cups drained, cooked or canned cannellini beans or other large white beans
1 1/2 cups bean cooking liquid or chicken stock
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 cloves garlic or shallots, sliced lengthwise paper-thin
method: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 hours, changing the water 2 or 3 times; drain.
Heat the oil in a cazuela or deep sauté pan over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic about 4 minutes without colour.
Set the cod on the onions and cook 5 minutes in all, turning once; lift it out.
Add the beans (rinsed if canned) and their liquid or stock, season lightly, cover and simmer gently 20 minutes.
Mash about 3/4 cup of the beans roughly and return them, then add the cod in large flakes, removing any bones. Heat 5 minutes.
Swirl the pan repeatedly until the stew thickens and comes together; season and stir in the vinegar.
Meanwhile fry the sliced garlic in 1/4 inch of oil over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp; drain on paper towels.
Serve in warm soup plates topped with garlic chips, a guindilla (or peperoncino) and parsley leaves.

title: Shrimp Tartine with Fava Bean, Almond, and Mint Pesto
chef: David Kinch, Manresa, Los Gatos
ingredients: For the fava bean, almond, and mint pesto:
1 cup shelled young fava beans (about 50, from 1 pound unshelled)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 olive oil–packed anchovy fillet, finely chopped
About 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil
Few drops of fresh lemon juice (optional)
36 large shrimp in the shell (1 1/2 to 2 pounds)
12 slices coarse country bread, toasted, preferably over a wood fire
Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
method: Blanch the favas in boiling salted water about 30 seconds, cool in cold water and slip off their skins (can be done a day ahead).
Pound the garlic, mint and a pinch of salt to a rough paste in a mortar, then work in the anchovy and almonds; or pulse them together in a processor, adding a spoon of oil if needed.
Move to a processor, add the favas and pulse briefly, keeping some texture. Pulse in the cheese.
With the motor running, trickle in the oil until it is pesto-like, then season with salt and lemon juice.
Drop the shrimp into a large pan of boiling salted water, take it off the heat, cover and leave 3 to 5 minutes until pink and opaque.
Drain, then peel and devein while warm.
Spread each toast thickly with pesto, top with 3 shrimp, drizzle with oil, grind over pepper and serve.

title: Pan-Roasted Halibut with Melted Leeks and Meyer Lemon–Caper Butter
chef: Craig Stoll, Delfina Restaurant, San Francisco
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Champagne or white wine vinegar
1 fresh or 2 small dried bay leaves
3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons (7 ounces) unsalted butter, at room temperature, cut into 2-inch cubes
method: Use only the leek whites. Trim the roots, quarter lengthwise and cut into 3/4-inch squares. Swish in cold water, let settle 5 minutes and lift the floating leeks out.

Barely cover the leeks with water in a 10-inch pan, add a pinch of salt, boil, then simmer briskly 10 to 15 minutes until about 1/2 inch of water is left. Stir in the 4 tablespoons butter; cook a little longer with extra water if still crunchy.
Pat the capers dry and fry in the shimmering olive oil 1 to 2 minutes until puffed and crisp; drain.
For the sauce, zest the lemons. In a 2-quart nonreactive pan combine the wine, vinegar, shallots, half the tarragon, thyme, bay, peppercorns, and the juice and rinds of 3 lemon halves.
Boil, then simmer on medium 15 to 20 minutes until nearly dry. Add the cream and reduce by half, 5 to 10 minutes.
On low heat whisk in the butter a cube or two at a time without letting it boil, then strain.
Stir in the remaining tarragon leaves, chopped, half the capers and the zest; season, adding juice from the reserved lemon half if needed. Keep warm over hot water.
Heat the oven to 325°F. Salt the halibut, set in melted butter in an ovenproof pan over medium heat and roast about 15 minutes until it just starts to flake.
Meanwhile boil the leeks with half the chives until the water is gone but they are still moist.
Plate the leeks, top with halibut, spoon over the sauce and finish with the remaining capers and chives.

title: Lasagna with Neapolitan Ragù
chef: Joyce Goldstein, San Francisco (chef, author)
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef brisket or boneless chuck, in one piece
1/2 pound boneless veal shoulder, in one piece
1/2 pound boneless pork shoulder, in one piece
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 (28-ounce) cans plum tomatoes with juice, hand chopped or pulsed in a food processor
Small pinch of chile pepper flakes (optional)
Meat stock or water, if needed
4 cups whole milk or half-and-half, heated
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 pound dried or 1 pound fresh lasagna noodles
Unsalted butter, at room temperature, cut into bits for topping
method: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, add the three meats and salt them; cook about 15 minutes until they release their juices.
Add the onion, lower to medium and cook up to 15 minutes, turning the meat, until browned and the onion is golden.
Add the wine and cook about 10 minutes until absorbed. Add the tomatoes and chile flakes, partly cover and simmer on low 2 1/2 hours, stirring often and adding stock if it threatens to catch.
When thick and the meat is very tender, chop the meat small, return it to the sauce and season.

For the cream sauce, cook the butter and flour on low about 3 minutes without colouring, whisk in the hot milk, bring nearly to a boil, then cook on low about 8 minutes until thick. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9-by-12-by-3-inch (or 10-by-13-by-3-inch) dish.
Cook the noodles until almost al dente (about 3 minutes for fresh, refreshing them in cold water) and lay them flat on towels.
Layer a thin coat of ragù, then noodles, ragù, cream sauce and Parmesan; repeat, starting and finishing with noodles. Dot with butter.
Bake 45 to 60 minutes until bubbling at the edges, rest 10 minutes and cut into squares.

title: Juniper-Scented Chicken Liver Pâté on Crostini
chef: Evan Kleiman, Angeli Caffe, Los Angeles
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling (optional)
1 or 2 juniper berries, crushed in a mortar
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Slice the bread thinly, lay on a tray, drizzle with oil and toast about 5 minutes, just until starting to colour. Cool.
Trim the livers of fat, membrane and any green spots.
Heat the oil in a sauté pan over medium heat, add the livers, prosciutto, tomato sauce and juniper, season and cook 5 to 8 minutes until the livers just firm up, still slightly pink inside.
Cool a few minutes, then lift the mixture onto a board with a slotted spoon and chop to a coarse purée. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve warm in a bowl surrounded by the crostini, or spread on the toasts.

title: Penne with Asparagus, Prosciutto, and Peppers
chef: Michael Romano, Union Square Cafe, New York
ingredients: 2 ounces thinly sliced prosciutto, cut into 1/4-inch-wide strips
method: Broil the peppers 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred all over. Cover in a bowl for about 10 minutes, then peel, seed and dice.
Snap off the woody asparagus ends, peel the stalks up to about 2 inches from the tip and cut on the diagonal into 2-inch pieces.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the asparagus 2 to 3 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Add the peppers and garlic for about 1 minute, pour in the stock, bring to a boil and take off the heat.
Boil the penne in salted water about 8 minutes, until a little short of al dente, and drain.
Add the pasta and thyme to the skillet over medium heat and cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until al dente.
Mix in the prosciutto, 1/3 cup of the cheese, the remaining butter, salt and pepper.
Serve in a warm bowl topped with the rest of the cheese.

title: Warm Kabocha Squash Salad with Dandelion, Bacon, Roncal, and Pecans
chef: Suzanne Goin, Lucques / A.O.C. / The Hungry Cat, Los Angeles
ingredients: 6 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon extra virgin olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2/3 pound apple wood–smoked bacon, in a single piece
1/4 pound Roncal, Manchego, or pecorino cheese
method: Heat the oven to 475°F. Halve, seed and peel the squash and cut it into 1/2-inch wedges.
Toss with 4 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons salt, pepper and the thyme, spread in one layer and roast about 20 minutes, turning halfway, until tender. Keep warm.
Drop the oven to 375°F and toast the pecans about 10 minutes until fragrant; toss with 1 teaspoon oil and a pinch of salt.
Cut the bacon into 3/8-inch slices, then into 3/8-inch-wide lardons.
Whisk the vinegar with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Put the dandelion greens in a big bowl.
Heat a large pan on high 1 minute and cook the bacon about 5 minutes, until just browning but still chewy. Keep 2 tablespoons fat.
On medium heat stir in the shallots, then take off the heat and swirl in the vinaigrette to warm it.
Add the squash and the bacon mixture to the greens, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper and toss gently.
Layer half the salad on a platter with half the cheese shaved over and half the pecans; repeat and serve warm.

title: Lentil Soup with Fennel Sausages
chef: Frank Stitt, Highlands Bar and Grill / Bottega / Chez Fonfon, Birmingham
ingredients: 1 large Vidalia or other sweet onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 red bell peppers, seeded and cut into 1/4-inch dice
1/2 fennel bulb, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 1/2 cups Le Puy lentils or brown lentils, rinsed
Bouquet garni of several fresh thyme sprigs, 1 leek top (optional), and 2 bay leaves, tied in a cheesecloth bundle
2 quarts spring water or chicken stock
1/2 cup Carmenère or other dry red wine
Fruity extra virgin olive oil for serving
Chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, thyme, or marjoram for garnish
method: Soften the onion, carrots, peppers and fennel in 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
Turn the heat to high, add the garlic and chile and cook 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, bouquet garni and water or stock, salt, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered on medium-low about 45 minutes until very tender.
Meanwhile brown the sausages in the last tablespoon of oil over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes.
Pour in the wine, cover and cook on low about 10 minutes until cooked through.
Discard the bouquet garni, slice the sausages and add them with their pan juices to the soup; adjust seasoning.
Serve very hot with a drizzle of fruity oil and chopped herbs.

title: Duck Basteeya
chef: Mourad Lahlou, Aziza, San Francisco
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Leaves from 1/2 bunch flat-leaf parsley, chopped
1/4 cup loosely packed fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
2 1/2 cups duck stock, chicken stock, or water
1/2 cup clarified butter, melted and cooled
1 1/2 teaspoons ground cinnamon, plus more for sprinkling
12 feuilles de brik or phyllo sheets (see note)
4 teaspoons fresh lemon juice or red wine vinegar
method: Salt the duck legs and brown them in the grape seed oil in a hot heavy pan over medium-high heat, about 5 minutes per side.

In a wide heavy pot, soften the onions in the olive oil over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes. Add the butter, herbs, cinnamon stick, saffron, ginger, turmeric, 1 tablespoon salt and 1 1/2 teaspoons pepper and cook 1 minute.
Lay in the duck skin side up, add the stock, boil, then cover and simmer on medium-low about 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Toast the almonds at 375°F about 10 minutes until golden; cool. Then raise the oven to 400°F.
Lift out the duck and discard the cinnamon stick. Boil the liquid hard until very thick, then on medium-low stir in the eggs about 5 minutes until firmly scrambled. Drain and cool.
Shred the duck meat into bite-size pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Grind the almonds coarsely and mix with the orange blossom water, 1/4 cup clarified butter, sugar and 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, then fold in the duck and eggs.
Keep the pastry covered. Brush one sheet generously with clarified butter, place 1/2 cup filling near the edge, fold over, roll halfway, tuck in the sides and finish rolling. Repeat.
Bake seam side down about 10 minutes until golden; cool 5 minutes.
Dress the arugula with the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Trim the roll ends, halve each on the diagonal, dust with icing sugar and cinnamon, and stand them around a mound of arugula on each plate.

title: Wild Salmon with Dolcetto Wine Sauce, Chanterelles, and Brussels Sprout Leaves
chef: Paul Bartolotta, Bartolotta Ristorante di Mare, Las Vegas
ingredients: For the Dolcetto wine sauce base:
1 pound salmon bones, rinsed and cut into small pieces
2 1/4 cups Dolcetto or other medium-bodied red wine
To finish the Dolcetto wine sauce:
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces
6 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into 6 pieces
5 ounces chanterelles, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
5 ounces porcini or other wild mushrooms or cremini mushrooms, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices or pieces
method: Heat the oven to 450°F. Melt the butter in a roasting pan, toss in the salmon bones and roast about 20 minutes until golden. Remove the bones; lower the oven to 400°F.
On the stovetop over medium heat, caramelize the shallots about 5 minutes, then add the onion, carrot, celery, bay, thyme and peppercorns for 5 to 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and vinegar until the vinegar cooks off, then add the wine and bones and reduce by three-quarters, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the stock, boil, then simmer uncovered 20 minutes. Strain (about 1 1/2 cups) and keep at a simmer.
For the finish, boil the red wine vinegar almost dry, then the balsamic almost dry, then add the wine and tomato paste and reduce by three-quarters.
Bring both mixtures to a boil and slowly whisk the base into the reduction; simmer on medium about 5 minutes to 1 cup.
Season, whisk in the cold butter piece by piece, strain and keep warm.
Salt the salmon and sear with the halved shallots in the oil in an ovenproof pan over high heat about 3 minutes until golden.
Flip, add the butter, thyme and bay, and roast about 4 minutes for barely translucent (7 for fully opaque).
At the same time, brown the butter in another ovenproof pan, add the mushrooms and sprout leaves, salt, and roast about 5 minutes until tender.
Mound the vegetables on warm plates, spoon sauce around, set the salmon on top, baste with the pan butter and garnish with shallots, thyme and bay.

title: Salad of Cornish Game Hen with Shiitake Mushroom Vinaigrette
chef: Charlie Trotter, Charlie Trotter's, Chicago
ingredients: Sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
6 ounces shiitake mushrooms, stems discarded and coarsely chopped
1/2 cup mushroom or vegetable stock, or as needed
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 425°F. Dry the hens, season, rub with oil and set breast up on a rack in a small roasting pan.
Roast 10 minutes, then lower to 325°F and roast 35 to 45 minutes more until the thigh juices run clear.
For the dressing, sweat the garlic and shallot in the oil over low heat about 5 minutes.
Add the shiitakes on medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, then the stock, reducing by half, about 2 minutes. Off the heat stir in the soy and lemon juice.
Blend until silky, adding stock to loosen if needed, and season.
Rest the hens 5 minutes, then split each lengthwise.
Toss the greens with 1/4 cup of the dressing. Plate a hen half beside a portion of salad, drizzle the rest of the dressing around, and finish with pepper and cranberries.

title: Roasted Chicken with Fingerling Potatoes and Fava Bean and Cipollini Onion Salad
chef: Laurent Manrique, Café de la Presse, San Francisco
ingredients: For the wine and stock reduction:
1 1/2 cups Grenache or other medium-bodied dry red wine
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 pound small cipollini onions (about 1 inch in diameter)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
1 tablespoon plus 1 1/2 teaspoons chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 ounces bacon, in a single piece
1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, stemmed and halved
4 tablespoons mixed chopped fresh herbs such as flat-leaf parsley, chervil, tarragon, and chives, in any combination
1 small head frisée, torn into bite-size pieces
method: Sweat the shallots in the butter on low about 5 minutes. Add the wine on high and reduce by three-quarters, about 5 minutes; add the stock and reduce by half, about 10 minutes, until it coats a spoon. Season (about 2 cups).
Brown the cipollini in foaming butter over medium heat about 5 minutes, add the water and cook about 5 minutes more until it evaporates and the onions are tender and browned. Season, cool and halve.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Mash the soft butter with 1 tablespoon parsley, the thyme and garlic, and season.
Loosen the chicken's breast and thigh skin from the cavity end without tearing it, spread the herb butter underneath and season the bird all over.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil and seasoning in a single layer in a roasting pan and set the chicken on top, breast up.
Roast about 1 hour, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 160°F.
Cut the bacon into 1/4-inch lardons and fry in a hot pan 3 to 4 minutes until crisp; drain.
Shell the favas, blanch about 30 seconds, cool in cold water and slip off their skins.
Rest the chicken under foil 15 minutes. Toss the potatoes with the remaining parsley and season.
Toss the onions, bacon, favas, tomatoes, herbs and frisée with the last tablespoon of oil and season.
Carve the chicken, serve over the potatoes on a warm platter, with the warmed sauce and the onion salad on the side.

title: Braised Shank of Beef
chef: Fergus Henderson, St. John, London
ingredients: 2 tablespoons rendered duck fat or unsalted butter
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
12 cloves garlic, peeled but left whole
8 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices
Bouquet garni of 6 fresh thyme sprigs, 3 fresh rosemary sprigs, 1/2 bunch fresh flat-leaf parsley, and 2 bay leaves, tied in a cheesecloth bundle
method: Heat the oven to 275°F.
Season the shank and brown it well on all sides in the hot duck fat over medium heat, about 10 minutes.
In a deep baking dish or Dutch oven, layer the shallots, garlic, shank, carrots, wine and bouquet garni.
Pour in stock until the ingredients are mostly submerged, with just the top showing, and cover tightly.
Braise 6 hours, until a knife tip slides into the meat with no resistance; if not, give it another 15 to 30 minutes and test again.
Season and serve straight from the dish.

title: Seared Tuna with Braised Cabbage and Roasted Mushrooms
chef: Douglas Keane, Cyrus and Healdsburg Bar and Grill, Healdsburg
ingredients: For the cabbage, mushrooms, and tuna:
1 head red cabbage, about 1 1/2 pounds, cored, halved, and thinly sliced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/4 cup finely minced, peeled green apple
1 cup Mencía or other dry red wine
3/4 pound cremini mushrooms, trimmed and quartered (about 2 cups)
2 pounds ahi tuna fillets, trimmed of any blood lines and sinew
method: Toast the spice-mix ingredients in a dry pan over low heat 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant, cool and grind finely. Use 1 tablespoon; store the rest.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss the cabbage with 1 tablespoon salt and the sugar.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large ovenproof pan on low and cook the bacon about 3 minutes to render.
Add the shallots, garlic and apple for about 5 minutes until soft, then the spice mix for 2 to 3 minutes.
Squeeze the cabbage dry by handfuls into the pan, stir in the wine and vinegar, cover and braise in the oven about 1 hour until soft and the liquid is gone.
Ten minutes before the end, brown butter lightly over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms, season and roast about 5 minutes until tender.
Spread the cabbage in a warm serving dish, top with the mushrooms and keep covered.
Season the tuna and sear in very hot oil over high heat 1 to 2 minutes per side, leaving it rare inside.
Slice across the grain, lay over the vegetables and serve. The cabbage can be made hours ahead and reheated at 350°F for about 15 minutes.

title: Barbecued Turkey Skewers with Caramelized Sage Onions
chef: Cindy Pawlcyn, Mustards Grill, Napa Valley
ingredients: 1/2 cup firmly packed dark brown sugar
2 tablespoons unsalted butter or extra virgin olive oil
12 to 16 cipollini or large pearl onions (about 1 inch in diameter), sliced
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Boil the water, pomegranate molasses, sugar, thyme, garlic, pepper and chile paste, stirring, then simmer 5 minutes. Pour into a large bowl and add the ice to cool.
Submerge the turkey thighs, cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
Mix the barbecue sauce ingredients. Soak bamboo skewers about 30 minutes if using.
Drain the turkey, cut the meat off the bone (skin on or off) into rough 1 1/2-inch cubes and thread loosely onto 4 skewers.
Set aside half the sauce for serving and coat the skewers with some of the rest while a grill heats to medium.
For the onions, cover and cook the butter, water, radishes, onions, shallots, sage, salt and pepper over medium heat 10 minutes; uncover on high and cook 3 to 4 minutes until caramelized.
Grill the skewers 8 to 12 minutes, turning often and basting with sauce, until browned and cooked through.
Boil the reserved sauce with the butter and 2 tablespoons wine until thick enough to coat, adding up to 2 tablespoons more wine if needed.
Serve the skewers with the onions, drizzled with some sauce and the rest on the side. No pomegranate molasses? Use 1/4 cup each light molasses and pomegranate juice.

title: Braised Duck Leg in Ragù with Chestnut Polenta and Green Olives
chef: Nate Appleman, Pulino's Bar and Pizzeria, New York
ingredients: 1/4 pound pancetta, in a single piece
1 1/2 cups Nebbiolo or other dry red wine
1 (28-ounce) can San Marzano tomatoes with juice
1 cup polenta, preferably Anson Mills brand
Extra virgin olive oil for serving
method: Salt the duck legs well, cover and refrigerate 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 275°F. Brown the legs skin side down in the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat about 5 minutes, then a minute or two on the other side. Remove.
Cut the pancetta into 1/4-inch lardons. Pour off half the fat and cook the onion and pancetta on medium about 5 minutes, until soft but not crisp.
Add the wine and reduce by half on high, about 5 minutes. Add the hand-crushed tomatoes with juice, the duck and the olives.
Cover and braise in the oven about 1 1/2 hours, until tender but not falling off the bone.
Meanwhile stir the polenta into the water in a heavy 2 1/2-quart pan, salt, and bring to a simmer over medium-high, stirring constantly 5 to 8 minutes until it thickens.
Cook on low, stirring often, about 1 hour until soft. Add the chestnut flour and cook about 10 minutes more; season and keep covered.
Loosen the polenta with hot water if stiff. Serve in warm soup plates topped with a duck leg, sauce and olives, and a good drizzle of oil.
Without chestnut flour, make plain polenta with 1 1/2 cups polenta in total.

title: Mixed Grill
chef: Christopher Gross, Christopher's and Crush Lounge, Phoenix
ingredients: 1 1/2 teaspoons coarsely ground mixed black and white peppercorns
1/2 pound beef tenderloin or flank steak, in a single piece
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 merguez or other sausages of choice
1 large russet potato, about 4 inches long
method: Whisk the sun-dried tomatoes, garlic and vinegar, then whisk in the oil slowly. Season with the peppercorns and salt.
Blanch the cabbage half in boiling salted water about 3 minutes, chill in cold water, drain, cut into 4 wedges and pat dry.
Heat a grill to medium. Brush the lamb, chicken and beef with oil and season.
Peel the potato and cut into 1/4-inch matchsticks; soak 5 minutes, drain and dry.
Fry in 2 inches of canola oil at 375°F about 8 minutes, stirring, until golden. Drain and keep warm.
Grill, turning once: lamb 3 to 5 minutes a side for medium; chicken 3 to 5 minutes a side until opaque; tenderloin 2 to 3 minutes a side for medium-rare (flank about 4).
Grill the sausages about 8 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Set a cabbage wedge on each plate with greens and a tomato quarter, cut or slice the beef, and arrange all the meats on top.
Top with the fries and pass the vinaigrette. Meats can be grilled an hour ahead and reheated at 350°F for about 5 minutes.
protein: lamb chops, beef, chicken, merguez sausage

title: Roasted Pork Shoulder with Pan-Roasted Carrots
chef: Michael Leviton, Lumière, Newton, Massachusetts
ingredients: 1 bottle (750 ml) Pinotage or other dry red wine
Grated zest and juice of 1/2 orange
1/2 fresh bay leaf or 1 whole dried bay leaf
1 (2 1/2- to 3-pound) boneless pork shoulder roast, rolled and tied
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds carrots (about 10 medium), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons nonpareil capers, rinsed and drained
3 tablespoons golden raisins, soaked in hot water to cover for 10 minutes and drained
method: Mix the wine, orange zest and juice, garlic, thyme, bay, cinnamon, juniper and cloves in a nonreactive dish. Add the pork, cover and refrigerate 2 days, turning occasionally.
Heat the oven to 500°F. Lift out the pork (keep the marinade), scrape and dry it, season well and set fat side up in a lightly oiled snug roasting pan.
Roast 30 minutes, then lower to 300°F and roast 2 1/2 to 3 hours until the centre reads 175°F.
Strain the marinade and simmer 30 to 40 minutes until reduced to 1/3 to 1/2 cup.
Brown half the carrots in 2 tablespoons sizzling butter over medium-high heat 4 to 5 minutes until tender (add a splash of water on low if needed). Season, drain and repeat with the rest.
Rest the pork under foil about 15 minutes and skim the fat from the pan juices.
Boil the reduced marinade, pan juices and stock over medium-high heat 10 to 15 minutes to halve. Season, sharpen with vinegar or enrich with butter if you like.
Reheat the carrots in the remaining tablespoon of butter with the capers, raisins and pine nuts; season and add the chives.
Untie and slice the pork and serve with the sauce and carrots.

title: Rustic Beef Stew with Prunes and Guajillo Chile Sauce
chef: Robert Del Grande, RDG + Bar Annie, Houston
ingredients: 6 guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded (see note)
4 cloves garlic, peeled but left whole
1/2 small fennel bulb, trimmed and coarsely chopped
1 tablespoon red wine vinegar or other mild vinegar
2 tablespoons fresh tarragon leaves, or 4 fresh tarragon sprigs
method: Bring the beef and water just to a boil in a 5-quart Dutch oven, skimming, then cover and simmer gently on medium-low about 2 hours until nearly cooked.
Remove the beef to cool. Boil the broth uncovered about 15 minutes to reduce to 3 cups, rest 5 minutes and skim off the fat.
Trim the cooled beef of fat and sinew and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Toast the chiles at 350°F about 15 minutes until lightly browned, soak in warm water about 30 minutes, drain and chop.
Simmer the raisins, garlic and fennel in the 3 cups broth, covered, 20 to 30 minutes until soft; cool.
Blend the broth mixture with the chiles, pine nuts, almonds, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth.
Melt the butter in the beef pot over medium-high heat until foaming and brown the beef and prunes about 5 minutes.
Add the sauce carefully (it spits), then cook at a bare simmer uncovered 30 to 40 minutes until the beef is tender, thinning with water if needed.
Serve topped with pine nuts, almonds, tarragon and a pinch of coarse salt. New Mexico red (6) or ancho (4) chiles can stand in for guajillos.

title: Roast Rack of Lamb with Creamy Rice with Parsnips
chef: Dan Barber, Blue Hill, New York
ingredients: 1/2 pound parsnips (2 small), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch chunks (about 1 cup)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 3/4 cups vegetable stock, or as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Simmer the rice and water, covered on low, 17 to 20 minutes until the water is absorbed (about 3 cups cooked).
Cook the seasoned parsnips gently in the oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, without colouring.
Add 1 1/2 cups stock and simmer uncovered 5 to 10 minutes until tender and the liquid has halved. Blend smooth (about 1 cup), adding stock if too thick.
Season the lamb well and sear fat side down in hot oil over medium-high heat 3 to 4 minutes, then about 4 minutes on the other side.
Roast on a tray about 20 minutes for medium-rare, then rest under foil 10 to 15 minutes.
Simmer the cooked rice with the remaining 1 1/4 cups stock, stir in the parsnip purée and heat through; season.
Cut the racks into chops and serve with the rice sprinkled with chives.

title: Grilled Pork Chops with Dried Cherry, Bacon, and Vidalia Onion Conserve
chef: Ben Barker, Magnolia Grill, Durham, North Carolina
ingredients: 4 (3/4-pound) pork rib chops, preferably from pasture-raised pork
For the dried cherry, bacon, and Vidalia onion conserve:
1 1/2 cups Touriga Nacional or other fruity red wine
1/4 pound slab bacon, in a single piece
2 (6-ounce) Vidalia or other sweet onions, thinly sliced
2 tablespoons unsulfured light molasses, or 1/4 cup pomegranate molasses
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon aniseeds or fennel seeds, coarsely ground in a mortar or spice grinder
1 teaspoon coriander seeds, coarsely ground in a mortar or spice grinder
method: Trim and dry the chops, rub them with the cut garlic, salt lightly, cover and chill at least 2 hours or overnight. Take out 30 minutes before grilling.
Warm the cherries in the wine to just below a simmer, cool, then drain, keeping cherries and wine separately.
Cut the bacon into 1/4-inch lardons and fry over medium heat 3 to 5 minutes until browned but tender; drain.
Keep 1/4 cup fat in the pan, add the onions and bay leaves for 2 minutes, then cover and cook on very low about 20 minutes until soft.
Add the molasses and vinegar and boil on medium, then add the cherry wine and simmer about 10 minutes until mostly absorbed.
Stir in the bacon and cherries, season with salt and plenty of pepper, and keep warm.
Set up a grill for indirect cooking over medium heat. Mix the ground seeds, pepper and oil and rub over the chops.
Grill over the fire 2 minutes, rotate 90 degrees for 2 more minutes, then move to the cool side, cover and cook 6 to 8 minutes for medium.
Rest under foil 4 to 5 minutes and serve with the warm conserve. The conserve can be made hours ahead; add the bacon at the end.

title: Grilled Lamb Skewers with Xinomavro and Honey Glaze
chef: Tom Douglas, Dahlia Lounge / Palace Kitchen / Lola, Seattle
ingredients: 2 teaspoons dried Greek or other oregano
2 pounds boneless lamb from leg, cut into 1-inch chunks
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Soak bamboo skewers 30 minutes if using.
Mix the garlic, oregano, lemon zest, salt and pepper, then whisk in the oil.
Thread the lamb on the skewers, lay in a dish, coat with the marinade, cover and refrigerate 6 hours to overnight.
For the glaze, brown the shallots in the butter over medium-high heat about 3 minutes, add the wine and boil hard 20 to 30 minutes to a syrup (about 1/3 cup); watch it closely.
Whisk in the honey, salt and some pepper, cook 1 minute and cool. It keeps 2 days chilled; use at room temperature.
Heat a grill to medium and let the lamb come to room temperature.
Shake off the marinade, season, and grill 7 to 8 minutes for medium-rare, turning often.
Near the end brush with the glaze and turn to caramelize it lightly.
Toss the parsley with a squeeze of lemon, the oil, salt and pepper, and pile it over the skewers on a warm platter.
